newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French three-month interest rate futures surged with bond futures on Monday, driven by renewed optimism and a return of foreign invstors after weekend opinion polls showed a more convincing centre-right election victory.

Traders said the two weekend polls showing some of the best results for the centre-right since the parliamentary election campaign started had boosted the market early and short covering produced another surge before the MATIF close.
June PIBOR ended 16 basis points higher and the June 10-year bond future rose strongly too, both making further gains in a late push attributed by traders to short covering.

Traders said the the June 10-year future rose partly on the back of PIBOR but gathered its own momentum once it neared the psychologically important 130.30 level, its day high at MATIF close of business.

With the stock market rise and a firm opening in the U.S. bond and stock markets, optimism spread and the contract could push further ahead on Tuesday, with a key target of 130.32, one trader at a French bank said.
The cash market also performed strongly, with yields on the benchmark 10-year government bond -- 5.50 percent April 2007 -- dropping to 5.59 percent late in the day from 5.67 last Friday.
The 10-year OAT also outperformed its German equivalent, with the yield spread moving to minus 12 from minus nine basis points.

An IFOP poll released on Saturday showed the ruling RPR and UDF parties' lead over the left growing, predicting the combined centre-right winning 41 percent of the vote against 35.5 percent for the Socialists/Communist combination.

The score for the centre-right was one of the strongest since polling got going in earnest and a SOFRES poll released on Sunday showed gains on the right as well, with 39.5 percent for the centre-right parties. This was neck-and-neck with the two left parties combined but well ahead on the, albeit less reliable, front of seat attribution in the National Assembly.
